brief: My partner and I are sorting out our money before the new year, and I want a single page showing where October's take-home pay went. Take-home was £3,850. Rent £1,260. Groceries £540. Childcare £480. Utilities and broadband £235. Transport £190. Eating out and takeaways £210. Subscriptions and streaming £68. Health and pharmacy £85. Savings £400. Everything else £382. Show each category as its share of the whole, with the pound amount and the percentage written on it, biggest first. At the top, put one plain sentence on what the three biggest add up to and one on how much we saved and what share of take-home that is. Check the figures add up to £3,850 and say so on the page. We will read it on our phones tonight on the sofa and I will print it for the fridge, so it has to make sense in black and white too. Make savings a calm green called Sage, #6B8F71, so it stands out. Our goal for November is eating out and subscriptions together under £250, so show how far over or under that October was.

I'm presenting the browser section of our Valmora market review on Thursday, projected in the boardroom, so the page has to be readable from the back of the room. Share of page views by browser in Valmora, third quarter 2026, with third quarter 2025 in brackets: Kestrel 41.2% (38.5%), Marlin 27.8% (29.9%), Plover 14.6% (13.1%), Lumen 8.9% (10.8%), Orrin 4.1% (4.9%), all others 3.4% (2.8%). The source is the Valmora Telecom Regulator's open traffic panel, published 2026-10-12, covering 6.2 million devices. Show the current split, with each browser's change in points against last year beside it, and lead with one sentence of what changed: Kestrel's lead over Marlin grew from 8.6 to 13.4 points. Colour Kestrel in deep teal, #0F6E6E, and keep the others quiet greys so it is obvious who is ahead. Put the method notes (how the panel counts a device, why mobile and desktop are combined) in an appendix the board can skip, and do not let them crowd the main view. Give it the title Browser share in Valmora, Q3 2026.

Pennywhistle, our meal-planning app, handled 13,600 support tickets this quarter and I have to explain where they came from at tomorrow's ops review. I will walk through it on my laptop and then paste the link into the team chat. Tickets by channel, July to September 2026 (this quarter, then last quarter): Email 4,820 (5,100). Live chat 3,960 (3,200). Phone 2,140 (2,600). In-app form 1,730 (1,300). Social media 610 (700). Community forum 340 (360). Median first reply this quarter: email 3 h 10 min, live chat 2 min, phone 45 sec, in-app form 1 h 25 min, social 52 min, forum 6 h. Show each channel's volume and share of the total, how it moved against last quarter in tickets and in percent, and put the first-reply time next to it so the slow channels stand out. Lead with the two channels that grew most. The sentence that should show when the link is shared: Pennywhistle support, Q3 2026: 13,600 tickets, with chat and in-app up and phone down. Nothing else is needed, no methodology section.

Residents keep asking me where the city's electricity comes from, so I need a handout page for the open day at Halvern Central Library on Saturday 14 November, printed on A4 and also opened on the library's wall screen. I am the city's sustainability officer. Share of electricity supplied to Halvern, 2026 so far (January to September, with 2021 in brackets): Natural gas 31% (33%), Wind 24% (12%), Hydro 14% (15%), Solar 11% (4%), Biomass 8% (7%), Coal 7% (24%), Imported from the national grid 5% (5%). Show the mix now beside the mix in 2021, with renewables (wind, hydro, solar, biomass) clearly grouped, so a visitor sees that renewables rose from 38% to 57%. Our council target is 70% renewable by 2030, so show how far there is to go. Write it for people who are not experts, in short sentences, in British English, with no jargon, and explain on the page what each source is in one line. Use Charcoal, #3B3F45, for coal and gas and a different green for each renewable source, with Wind as Meadow, #4C9F70. Put the data source (the Halvern Grid Operator's monthly reports) and the note that 2026 is nine months only in a small appendix at the end.

Headcount review, Thursday 12 November at 14:00, leadership team in the big meeting room with the page projected, and I am the People lead at Brantley Freight who has to run it. Headcount on 1 October 2026 against the plan we set in January (department: actual, plan): Engineering 84, 90. Sales 52, 50. Operations 47, 47. Customer Success 31, 34. Product 22, 24. Marketing 18, 20. Finance 14, 14. People 9, 10. Legal 4, 4. Company total is 281 against a plan of 293, so 12 roles are open. We can fund only 8 of those 12 hires before the end of the year, and the meeting has to decide which departments get them. Show every department's actual beside its plan, sorted from the biggest shortfall in people to the biggest surplus, with the gap in people and in percent, and flag any department at least 10% under plan. Make it plain that Sales is the only department over plan. Keep it to a single page with the total at the top, and a short line under the list reminding the room that 8 of 12 is the limit. Use Harbour Blue, #1F4E79, for actual and a light grey for plan.

On-call handover needs a page I can open on my phone between meetings and still read in ten seconds. Uptime in percent for the week Monday 26 October to Sunday 1 November 2026, by day from Monday to Sunday, then the weekly figure for the last eight weeks, oldest first, the last being that same week. Checkout: 100, 100, 99.2, 100, 100, 100, 100; weeks 99.95, 99.98, 99.91, 99.97, 99.99, 99.93, 99.96, 99.89. Search: 100, 100, 100, 98.1, 100, 100, 100; weeks 99.95, 99.92, 99.97, 99.90, 99.96, 99.94, 99.91, 99.73. Login: 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 99.6, 100; weeks 99.99, 99.97, 99.98, 99.99, 99.96, 99.98, 99.97, 99.94. Notifications: 100, 97.4, 100, 100, 100, 100, 99.8; weeks 99.82, 99.76, 99.88, 99.71, 99.80, 99.85, 99.79, 99.60. Our target is 99.9% a week. For each service give a row of seven day cells shaded by that day's uptime, the week's number, and its eight-week trend, so I can see at once which services missed target and whether that is a one-off or a slide. Colour any figure green (#2E8B57) at 99.9 or above, amber (#D98E04) below 99.9, and red (#C0392B) below 99.

I run a small tea shop called The Copper Kettle and my accountant and I go through the numbers on a laptop at my desk this Saturday morning. I want one page that shows four measures for October 2026, each with its current value big, how it moved against September, and its last twelve months drawn as a small trend, with the best and worst month marked on it. Months run November 2025 to October 2026. Revenue in £ thousand: 21, 34, 16, 15, 17, 19, 20, 18, 17, 19, 22, 27. Orders: 640, 980, 470, 450, 520, 560, 590, 540, 510, 560, 640, 780. Conversion rate in percent of visits that buy: 2.8, 3.4, 2.5, 2.4, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8, 2.6, 2.5, 2.7, 2.9, 3.2. Repeat customers in percent of orders: 31, 29, 33, 34, 34, 35, 35, 36, 36, 37, 37, 38. October revenue target was £25k, so show whether we beat it. Add a plain one-line verdict for each measure (up, down or flat) and a sentence at the top on how October went overall. Draw the trend lines in Copper, #B87333. My accountant will open the same page on her phone afterwards, so keep it readable on a small screen.

I started a ten-week half-marathon plan and want a month summary page for October 2026 that I can open on my phone after a run and send to my coach, Dev, as a link. Weekly figures for the four weeks starting Monday 5, 12, 19 and 26 October: Workouts 4, 5, 3, 5. Distance run in km 21, 28, 14, 31. Resting heart rate in beats per minute 58, 57, 58, 56. Average sleep in hours 6.8, 7.1, 6.4, 7.3. Morning weight in kg 78.4, 78.1, 78.0, 77.6. My goals for the month were 16 workouts, 90 km, resting heart rate below 57, sleep at 7.0 hours or more, and weight heading to 77.5 kg by 30 November. Week three I had a cold, which explains the dip, so please mark that week on the page. For each metric show the month total or average, the goal, whether I hit it, and the four-week trend, so I can see what moved. Put the strongest result first and the one that missed worst last. Keep the tone encouraging and the colours soft, with Lagoon, #2A9D8F, as the main one. Sentence for the link preview: October in numbers: 17 workouts and 94 km run, with a cold in week three.

We finally have the October survey results for Marrow & Co., our vegetable-box delivery, and I need to share them with the operations team by pasting a link into our team chat, where most will open it on their phones. The question was: Overall, how satisfied are you with your box? We ask it every quarter. Share of answers in each wave (Oct 2025, Jan 2026, Apr 2026, Jul 2026, Oct 2026): Very satisfied 31%, 33%, 36%, 38%, 41%. Satisfied 40%, 39%, 38%, 37%, 35%. Neutral 14%, 13%, 12%, 12%, 11%. Dissatisfied 10%, 10%, 9%, 8%, 8%. Very dissatisfied 5%, 5%, 5%, 5%, 5%. The October wave had 1,284 replies. Make the latest wave the main view, showing each answer's share, and beside each answer its path across the five waves so people can see which answers grew and which shrank. Add a line for the two satisfied answers together, 76% now against 71% a year ago. Two customer comments belong at the bottom, in the customers' own words: "Nothing arrived bruised and the recipe cards finally make sense." and "Twice this month the box came a day late." Use Beetroot, #8E2C48, for the very satisfied answer and keep the others in muted tones.

Our nightly tests got worse over the last ten days and I have to decide at Monday's stand-up, projected on the team room screen, whether we pause feature work for a stabilisation week. I lead the checkout platform team at Quillfeather. The suite has 2,400 tests. Nightly runs (date: passed / failed / skipped / duration in minutes): Oct 27: 2371 / 6 / 23 / 18.4. Oct 28: 2372 / 5 / 23 / 18.9. Oct 29: 2369 / 8 / 23 / 19.6. Oct 30: 2370 / 7 / 23 / 19.2. Oct 31: 2366 / 9 / 25 / 21.3. Nov 1: 2361 / 12 / 27 / 22.8. Nov 2: 2358 / 14 / 28 / 24.1. Nov 3: 2365 / 8 / 27 / 24.5. Nov 4: 2350 / 21 / 29 / 26.7. Nov 5: 2354 / 18 / 28 / 27.2. Our limit is 20 minutes and no more than 10 failures. The tests that fail most are checkout_refund_flow, sync_offline_queue and export_large_report. Show how many passed, failed and skipped on each night, the trend in how long each run took against the 20-minute limit, and which nights broke either limit. Finish with a one-line recommendation on the stabilisation week. Pass is green, #2F9E44, fail is red, #D6336C, skipped is Slate, #6B7280.

Please put together the cloud cost page for Thursday's finance review at Lantern Row, where the CFO and our head of engineering will have it projected and talk through it. Monthly bill in thousands of US dollars, May to October 2026, by service (May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct): Compute 18.4, 19.1, 19.8, 21.5, 24.9, 26.3. Database 9.2, 9.3, 9.5, 9.9, 10.2, 10.4. Storage 4.1, 4.3, 4.6, 4.9, 5.2, 5.5. Network transfer 3.8, 3.9, 4.4, 4.2, 5.1, 5.8. Observability 2.6, 2.7, 3.3, 3.6, 3.9, 4.2. GPU inference 1.9, 3.2, 5.6, 8.4, 11.7, 14.1. The monthly budget is 55 thousand. Show each month's bill split by service so the growth is visible, mark the month we crossed the budget, and give each service's six-month total and its share of the 309.5 thousand overall. The point to land is that GPU inference grew from 5% of the bill to 21% in six months and drove nearly half of the rise. The decision for the room is which service gets a spending cap first. Keep the main view to that story and put the per-service figures in an appendix the room can skip. Use Marigold, #E8A33D, for GPU inference and cool greys and blues for the rest.

As secretary of the Ashgrove Allotment Society I have to publish the result of the chair election from our annual meeting on 22 October 2026, and the committee wants it printed on one A4 sheet for the minutes and pinned on the noticeboard at the gate. Eligible members: 164. Ballots returned: 127, of which 2 were spoiled and 4 abstained, leaving 121 valid votes for the three candidates. Marguerite Oyelaran 61. Tobias Lindqvist 38. Jun Hasegawa 22. Under rule 9 the chair needs more than half of the valid votes, otherwise there is a run-off between the top two, and a turnout of at least a quarter of members is needed for the vote to count. Make the page declare the winner plainly, show each candidate's votes and share of the valid votes, say whether the majority rule and the turnout rule were met, and show turnout as a share of the 164. Add a line with the margin between first and second. Write in British English, in a formal but warm tone, in the society's green, Fern, #3F7D4E. The sentence for when the link is shared: Ashgrove Allotment Society chair election 2026: Marguerite Oyelaran elected with 61 of 121 valid votes.
